\subsection*{Gaussian Space --- Noise --- Continuous Bounds: Results}

\begin{lemma}[Integral formula for the real $L^p$ norm]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.toReal_eLpNorm_ofReal_eq_integral}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.toReal_eLpNorm_ofReal_eq_integral}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be a measure space, let $f:X\to\mathbb R$, and let $p>0$. If
$f$ belongs to $L^p(\mu)$, then its $L^p$ norm is $\left(\int_X
|f(x)|^p\,d\mu(x)\right)^{1/p}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Gaussian two-function inequality for continuous functions]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussian_two_function_continuous}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussian_two_function_continuous}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.boolean_two_function_positiveOffsets, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.correlatedGaussianMeasure, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianPairTorusMap, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianTorusMap, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.normalizedCubeBlocks, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.tendsto_booleanBlockExpectation_real, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.innerProduct_noiseOp_eq_weighted_sum, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseKernel, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseKernel_sum_left, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseKernel_sum_right, BooleanAnalysis.expect}
\difficulty{6}
Let $n$ be a natural number, and let $r,s,\rho\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $r>0$, $s>0$, $rs\le
1$, $0\le\rho\le 1$, and $\rho^2\le rs$. Suppose the two coordinate projections of the
joint Gaussian law of $(X,\rho X+\sqrt{1-\rho^2}Y)$ each have standard Gaussian product
measure as their distribution, where $X,Y$ are independent standard Gaussian vectors in
$\mathbb R^n$. For continuous real-valued functions $F,G$ on the torus $(\mathbb
R/\mathbb Z)^{\{1,\ldots,n\}\times\{0,1\}}$, one has
\[
\mathbb E\bigl[|F(T(X))|\,|G(T(\rho X+\sqrt{1-\rho^2}Y))|\bigr]
\le \left(\int |F(T(x))|^{1+r}\,d\gamma(x)\right)^{1/(1+r)}
\left(\int |G(T(x))|^{1+s}\,d\gamma(x)\right)^{1/(1+s)},
\]
where $\gamma$ is standard Gaussian product measure and $T(x)$ has coordinate $x_i$ in
the first torus block and $\sqrt2x_i$ in the second block, each taken modulo $1$.
\end{lemma}
